answerCheck.reason: A root must satisfy |x|<=100. On positive x, only positive sine half-waves can contribute. The first interval (0,pi) contributes one root besides the root at 0. For k=1,...,15, sin(x)-x/100 is negative at both endpoints 2k*pi and (2k+1)*pi and positive at its peak (2k+1/2)*pi<100. Strict concavity on each half-wave gives exactly two roots. The next positive half-wave starts at 32*pi>100. Odd symmetry gives 1+2*(1+30)=63.
